land.text: the Don-Donets steppe that Cliopatria's Khazaria shape of 888-895 still covers; the Pechenegs 'driven further west by the Khazars and Cumans by 889' arrive on it

predecessors.note: The Khazars page has the Khazars dominate 'the Volga-Don steppes' to c. 965 and dates the decline of Khazar control of the Middle Dnieper to 'the 880s'; no page opened says the Khazars gave up the Don-Dnieper steppe before 965, so the Pecheneg land is a contested zone against the Khazaria dossier (see ledger).

land.text: the Pontic steppe 'replaced' by Cumans and Torks after the weakened Pechenegs; Budjak (Bugeac) entered by the Cumans around 1068-1078

successors.note: The Pontic steppe passed to the Cumans and Torks long before 1091; at the end the Pechenegs held only the Danube fringe.

land.text: Paristrion (mostly modern Dobruja), where the Pechenegs had settled as allies and colonists and rebelled in the early 1070s; the survivors of Levounion were settled in depopulated areas of the Empire

correction.text: the steppe of the Don and the Donets, east of the Dnieper where the Magyars still sat

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. Infobox 'Dates 889-1091'; 'Driven further west by the Khazars and Cumans by 889'. The page gives no extent for 889; the Don-Donets steppe is the reading that puts them next to the Magyars they 'drove ... west of the Dnieper River by 892'. Infobox gives no area (compare: none possible); Khazars page 900 est. 1.0 M km2 for the Khazars alone.

correction.text: the steppe from the Don to the Dnieper, from which the Magyars were driven west by 892

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'the Pechenegs in turn drove the Magyars west of the Dnieper River by 892': the steppe up to the Dnieper is theirs. Soft; the page names the river, not a boundary.

correction.text: Patzinakia: the steppe from the Don to the Siret, eight provinces on both banks of the Dnieper

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Etelkoz page: 'A new Pecheneg invasion compelled the Magyars to leave Etelkoz and cross the Carpathian Mountains around 895'; Etelkoz is the land of the rivers 'Barouch', 'Koubou', 'Troullos', 'Broutos' and 'Seretos' (Spinei: the last three the Dniester, Prut and Siret), and in the 870s the Magyars held 'the lands between the Lower Danube and the Don River'. Pecheneg page: Patzinakia stretched west 'as far as the Siret River' (Constantine VII, c. 950), eight provinces, four on each side of the Dnieper. The shape is Don-Dnieper steppe plus Etelkoz; Crimea ('controlled ... the Crimean Peninsula' in the 9th and 10th centuries on the Pecheneg page; Khazars 'dominated the Crimea (650-c. 950)' on the Khazars page) is left out as unresolved.

correction.text: the steppe west of the Dnieper to the Siret, towards the Danube

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Khazars page: 'By 1043, Kimeks and Qipchaqs, thrusting westwards, pressured the Oguz, who in turn pushed the Pechenegs west'; Pecheneg page: after 1036 'the Pecheneg Horde moved towards the Danube' and 'other nomadic peoples replaced the weakened Pechenegs in the Pontic steppe: the Cumans and the Torks'. Only the land west of the Dnieper is kept; the split is the researcher's reading (Zaporizhzhya and Dnipropetrovsk straddle the river and are dropped whole).

correction.text: the former Patzinakia without the Bugeac (Budjak), which the Cumans entered around 1068-1078

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Cumans page: 'The Cumans first entered the Bugeac (Bessarabia) at some point around 1068-1078'. The Pechenegs keep the steppe between the Dnieper and the Dniester and Romanian Moldavia; the Danube fringe in Paristrion is a contested zone against the Byzantines from the early 1070s (ledger). The shape is soft.

ledger.note: 889: the Pechenegs, driven west by the Khazars and Cumans, are on the Pontic steppe. 'Driven further west by the Khazars and Cumans by 889'; infobox 'Dates 889-1091'. The page gives the year, not the land; the Don-Donets steppe is the reading.

region.text: the steppe between the Don and the Dnieper that Cliopatria draws in Khazaria

ledger.note: 889: the Khazar steppe and the Pecheneg steppe overlap. The Khazars page has Khazar rule over 'the Volga-Don steppes' to 965 and the Pecheneg page has the Pechenegs 'controlled much of the steppes of southeast Europe'; the Khazars 'attacked them from two directions' before 889 (Pecheneg page). No page dates a battle after 889, so the zone is a bridge (confidence 1) to show both claims.

region.text: the steppe up to the Dnieper

ledger.note: 892: the Magyars are pushed over the Dnieper. 'the Pechenegs in turn drove the Magyars west of the Dnieper River by 892'; the Khazars page adds a first Pecheneg attack on the Hungarians 'around 854'.

region.text: Etelkoz, between the Dnieper, the Lower Danube and the Siret

ledger.note: 895: the Pechenegs storm into Etelkoz and the Magyars leave for the Carpathian Basin. 'A new Pecheneg invasion compelled the Magyars to leave Etelkoz and cross the Carpathian Mountains around 895'; Simeon I of Bulgaria 'persuaded them to storm into Etelkoz'.

region.text: the steppe between the Don and the Dnieper

ledger.note: 969: the Khazar state ends, and with it the overlap of the two claims on the steppe. Khazars page: 'Sarkel fell in 965, with the capital city of Atil following, c. 968 or 969' (infobox 969); the pages do not give the land to the Pechenegs by name.

region.text: the steppe east of the Dnieper

ledger.note: 1043: the Oghuz push the Pechenegs west of the Dnieper. 'By 1043, Kimeks and Qipchaqs, thrusting westwards, pressured the Oguz, who in turn pushed the Pechenegs west'; after the 1036 defeat at Kiev 'the Pecheneg Horde moved towards the Danube'.

region.text: Paristrion on the southern bank of the Lower Danube

ledger.note: early 1070s: the Pechenegs of Paristrion rise against the Empire. 'It was not until the early 1070s that the Pechenegs launched an open rebellion'; they had been 'allowed to settle in the province as allies and colonists'; the province is 'mostly modern Dobruja'. The year 1072 is the researcher's rounding of 'early 1070s'.

1078: the Cumans hold the Bugeac. 'The Cumans first entered the Bugeac (Bessarabia) at some point around 1068-1078'; the page names no previous owner and the Pecheneg page puts the Pechenegs west of the Dnieper, so the counterpart is a reading.

29 April 1091: the Pechenegs are crushed at Levounion. 'On 29 April 1091, an invading force of Pechenegs was crushed by the combined forces of the Byzantine Empire'; the Pecheneg page: 'annihilated as an independent force in 1091'.

region.text: what remained of Patzinakia: the former Patzinakia without the Bugeac (Budjak), which the Cumans entered around 1068-1078 (as keyframe pechenegs_1078)

ledger.note: 1091: the Pecheneg state ends at Levounion. Survivors were captured; men of fighting age entered imperial service and the rest were settled in 'depopulated areas of the Empire' (Pecheneg page: the district of Moglena); the steppe was already Cuman, and the Cumans attacked the remnants again in 1094. [Reviewer ia-01-x, 2026-10-19] region aligned with keyframe pechenegs_1078: the Budjak was already Cuman from 1078 (ledger 7).

wars.name: Rus'-Pecheneg wars
wars.outcome: Wars and raids 'for more than two centuries' (920 war by Igor, 968 siege of Kiev, 972 Sviatoslav ambushed and killed, 1036 defeat under Yaroslav the Wise); the page records no border change, and after 1036 the Horde moved towards the Danube.
wars.note: Individual battles are dated on the Pecheneg page; none moves land on it.

wars.name: Battle of Levounion

zones.text: Paristrion and the Balkans plundered from the north

wars.outcome: 29 April 1091: Alexios I and the Cumans annihilate the Pechenegs; the survivors are settled inside the Empire.
wars.note: The page dates the invasion news to spring 1087.

wars.name: Pecheneg rebellion in Paristrion
wars.outcome: The Pechenegs settled in Paristrion rebelled in the early 1070s and were defeated in 1091.

certainty.note: A steppe confederation of eight provinces: no border is given by any page; every edge is approximate.

notes: New state (Cliopatria lacks the Pechenegs). Pages are thin on land: the keyframes are readings of 'between the Don and the Dnieper' (892), Etelkoz (895), 'as far as the Siret River' (Constantine VII, c. 950) and 'towards the Danube' (after 1036). Infobox gives no area, so no ratio is possible. The Khazaria dossier (ia-01-d) keeps the whole steppe to the Dnieper bend in Khazaria's shape to 964 (its note on khazaria_888); the 889-969 contest zone is a bridge for that overlap (confidence 1) and a gap-filler should open the Rus' Primary Chronicle pages or De Administrando Imperio to settle who held the Don-Dnieper steppe. Crimea is left out although the Pecheneg page says they 'controlled ... the Crimean Peninsula'. No capital is recorded on any page opened (the Kangar union page puts the Kangar capital in the Ulytau mountains, an earlier state). Gazetteer names used are all in the gazetteer (Budjak, Dobruja, Romanian Moldavia, Bessarabia, Pontic Steppe). Counterparts without dossiers of this group: magyars (Cliopatria 840-910), oghuz-turks (written by ia-01-e), cuman-kipchak-confederation (ia-01-g), kievan-rus (eu-16), khazaria (ia-01-d), byzantine-empire (eu-05). The Pecheneg communities in the Kingdom of Hungary (about 150 villages) are not drawn.
